Welcome to Regional Jet Center 
Our daily operation is supported by several specialized workshops, including the Sheet Metal Workshop . Here, we repair and restore aluminium components. When there's less repair work, you'll also be deployed on the hangar floor and work directly on the aircraft. 
What will you do? 
As a Sheet Metal Worker, you'll mainly start in the workshop, but you'll also regularly work on the aircraft in the hangar. You will work day, evening, night, and weekend shifts. Your tasks include: -

Reading and interpreting drawings and technical specifications; - 
Measuring and marking sheet metal according to drawings and templates; - 
Cutting, bending, punching, drilling, and straightening sheet metal using metalworking machines (incl. presses, punch machines, and CNC equipment); - 
Grinding and polishing seams, joints, and rough surfaces; - 
Forming various alloys according to drawing specifications; - 
Checking the quality of products and installations to ensure compliance; - 
Certifying the airworthiness of repaired aircraft components; - 
Maintaining a clean and safe working environment. Job requirements 
 - 
At least 3 years of relevant sheet-metal experience; - 
Knowledge of EASA laws and regulations; - 
Good command of both Dutch and English; - 
Holder of a Category B driving licence; - 
Must be an EU resident/citizen.
